method:
# Script reference discovery before/after experiment

Baseline: 8d85fbf0ba3530ef7265f75f2c62760a18c459eb (clean main). Candidate: codex/script-reference-performance, same base and content; only script discovery implementation and regression tests/benchmark change.

Hypothesis: repeated scalar-cell index maintenance, per-cell TLS acquisition and downgrade/upgrade work account for a material part of the previously sampled 12–25% reference-bookkeeping engine CPU share. Preserve discovery on each nested call because embedding hosts can replace shared global cells.

Qualifying comparisons are sequential, with no compilation/testing/sampling during timing. Same machine, release settings, fixed scenario/seed, players and viewport. Keep all raw results; label failed/occluded runs. Use paired ABBA order to reduce drift.

1. Fixed-work headless runs: 100 warmup + 600 measured ticks, real Tower, ClonkMars, Arso-Morf and 1,000-Stippel workloads; two runs per binary. Primary result: mean complete Engine::tick CPU time, including snapshot; report per-run variation and p95.
2. Separate deterministic-state checks at frames 101,200,300,400,500,600,700: compare canonical full EngineState JSON, including persisted fixed-point motion and RNG. This is baseline/candidate equivalence on these fixtures, not proof of full C++ parity.
3. Windowed app: 2-second warmup + 20-second measured windows, 1280x720 Metal and automatic frame skip, Tower, ClonkMars and 1,000 Stippels, two runs per binary. Report simulation/presentation throughput and latency. Simulation is normally paced: extra headroom need not increase capped FPS. Occluded windows are invalid for presentation comparisons.
4. Shared-global microbenchmark: 32 nested calls per entry with 0/128/512 globals, one live object reference per 16 globals; nine samples of 1,000 entries. Supportive mechanism measurement, not app speedup.

Clean full-app baseline preserved from the earlier investigation. Matching external headless/micro harness sources link baseline and candidate release libraries; record fingerprints, compiler commands and binary SHA-256. State capture and sampling run separately from qualifying timings. Full required local gates and merge-queue landing follow measurements.

## Observed fixture limitation

The first offline ClonkMars state comparison differed in landscape and mass movers. A second execution of the unchanged baseline also differed, including temperature. Investigation traced this to ClonkMars.c4d/System.c4g/TIME.c:38–41 calling native GetTime() in its temperature calculation; the native host exposes elapsed real time outside synchronized control modes, matching its documented C++ contract. Preserve the failed comparison and baseline repeat as evidence. ClonkMars remains an observational offline workload, not a fixed-work/full-state-equivalence result. The other three cases match all 21 complete state checkpoints; no values are normalized away.

clonkmars_limitation: Offline ClonkMars temperature calls native GetTime(), so elapsed real time changes temperature and downstream landscape/mass-mover state. The unchanged baseline also differs between runs. Retain all comparisons, but do not claim full-state equivalence for this scenario.
windowed_limitation: All 12 runs produced zero presentations; macOS reported the benchmark windows offscreen despite activation. These runs do not qualify for visible FPS or GPU performance comparisons. Retained offscreen simulation throughput excludes presentation cost.

offline_clock_oracle.behavior: FnGetTime returns an empty optional in synchronized control mode; otherwise it returns timeGetTime(). Verified directly from the pinned oracle in Git history.
